import trimesh, numpy as np
h = trimesh.load('exports/model.hanger.bb97b27d.stl')
grid = np.array([[-30,-15,0]]) # dummy
# probe: is point inside hanger? points in print coords (x, y=height rel tip, z=width)
tests = {
 'saddle x=30 z=0 y=crown-0.3 (expect False if chamfer cut)': (30, 41.0, 0.3),
 'saddle x=30 z=17 y=crown-0.5 (expect True)': (30, 39.7, 17),
 'saddle x=60 z=0 y=top-0.3': (60, 30.0, 0.3),
 'saddle x=60 z=8.5 y top': (60, 29.0, 8.5),
 'tenon x=0 y=10 z=8': (0, 10, 8),
 'neck x=15 y=21.5 z=17': (15, 21.5, 17),
}
for k,(x,y,z) in tests.items():
    print(k, h.contains(np.array([[x,y,z]]))[0])
# raycast inward from above at x=30, z=0: first hit y => actual crown edge height
for x in [0,15,30,45,60]:
    hits = h.ray.intersects_location([[x,60,0.0]],[[0,-1,0]], multiple_hits=True)
    print(f'x={x} z=0 hits y:', sorted([round(float(p[1]),2) for p in hits], reverse=True)[:3])
    hits = h.ray.intersects_location([[x,60,17.0]],[[0,-1,0]], multiple_hits=True)
    print(f'x={x} z=17 hits y:', sorted([round(float(p[1]),2) for p in hits], reverse=True)[:3])
